options.B: To determine the market price of pharmaceutical drugs
options.C: To uncover bottlenecks and improve institutional performance
options.D: To penalize junior staff for minor administrative mistakes

explanation: These audits identify inefficiencies in hospital systems to help leaders align daily practices with strategic goals. [learn more](GST321_U9_T4#GST321_U9_T4_h1)

question: How does innate immunity differ from adaptive immunity?

options.A: Innate immunity targets only viruses, while adaptive immunity targets bacteria
options.B: Innate immunity requires previous exposure, while adaptive immunity works at birth
options.C: Innate immunity relies only on antibodies, while adaptive immunity uses physical barriers
options.D: Innate immunity provides fast, general defense, while adaptive immunity is specific and builds memory

explanation: Innate defenses are present from birth and react the same way to all germs, whereas adaptive defenses target specific invaders and remember them for the future. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T83#GNS214_U1_T83_h2)

question: Why are youth-friendly corners important in primary health centers?

options.A: They provide free accommodation for visiting medical doctors
options.B: They serve as administrative offices for senior nurses
options.C: They store emergency surgical equipment for trauma cases
options.D: They reduce fear of judgment and encourage young people to seek care

explanation: Young people often avoid standard clinics due to stigma; youth-friendly spaces offer a welcoming and confidential environment. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h4)

question: Why must Nigerian nurses understand local laws and cultural norms regarding youth care?

options.A: To navigate conflicting standards between policy and community expectations
options.B: To legally fine parents who allow teenagers to visit clinics
options.C: To ensure that all cultural traditions override medical guidelines
options.D: To prevent any minor from receiving healthcare without a court order

explanation: Nurses often operate in spaces where national health goals clash with conservative local customs, requiring careful navigation. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T10#GNS312_U3_T10_h8)

question: How do communities of solution differ fundamentally from geographical communities?

options.A: They dissolve once the specific problem is resolved
options.B: They are officially registered with the ministry of health
options.C: They exclude traditional birth attendants and local leaders
options.D: They rely exclusively on digital communication channels

explanation: Goal-oriented groups are temporary structures tied to solving a particular issue rather than permanent residency. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of applying chlorhexidine gel to the newborn cord?

options.A: To reduce localized pain
options.B: To stop bleeding from the vessels
options.C: To accelerate the drying process
options.D: To prevent umbilical cord infection

explanation: Chlorhexidine is an antiseptic applied to the stump to prevent serious bacterial infections like omphalitis. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T60#GNS214_U1_T60_h4)

question: What is the term for converting an environmental stimulus into a cellular electrical signal?

options.A: Cortical mapping
options.B: Axonal regeneration
options.C: Sensory transduction
options.D: Synaptic transmission

explanation: Sensory transduction is the exact process where physical or chemical stimuli are transformed into electrical membrane potentials. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h4)

question: Why must nurses evaluate local beliefs before launching a new health campaign?

options.A: Local traditions dictate the required drug dosages
options.B: Community leaders manage all hospital finances
options.C: Ministry guidelines forbid launching unapproved programs
options.D: Fatalistic views can hinder the motivation to change

explanation: If a population believes health outcomes cannot be altered, they will lack the readiness to adopt new behaviors. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T14#GNS313_U2_T14_h3)

question: Through which structures does venous blood primarily drain out of the corpora cavernosa?

options.A: Subtunica venules
options.B: Internal pudendal veins
options.C: Dorsal lymphatic vessels
options.D: Deep dorsal vein

explanation: Subtunica venules drain blood from the erectile tissue, and their compression during erection stops outflow. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T4#GNS121_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why are indicator organisms used in water quality testing instead of screening for every pathogen?

options.A: Pathogens cannot survive long enough in a laboratory container
options.B: Testing for every specific pathogen is impractical and slow
options.C: Indicator bacteria give exact chemical measurements of heavy metals
options.D: Indicator organisms destroy all other harmful bacteria in the sample

explanation: Screening water for hundreds of different potential pathogens is too difficult, so reliable indicator bacteria are used instead. [learn more](GST114_U3_T3#GST114_U3_T3_h5)

question: A newly formed immunization outreach team is arguing over schedules and task assignments. What stage are they in?

options.A: Norming
options.B: Performing
options.C: Storming
options.D: Adjourning

explanation: Arguments and resistance over responsibilities are classic indicators of the storming stage in team development. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h2)

question: What is a major limitation of using serum albumin alone to assess protein status in a newly admitted patient?

options.A: It cannot be performed on pregnant women or older adults
options.B: It can be altered by acute inflammation and hydration changes
options.C: It only reflects the dietary intake of the past two hours
options.D: It requires expensive radioactive tracers to measure accurately

explanation: Albumin levels drop during infection or inflammation regardless of actual protein intake, complicating its interpretation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T19#GNS214_U1_T19_h5)

question: What is a key feature of Adolescent-Friendly Health Services (AFHS)?

options.A: High service fees to cover premium facility maintenance
options.B: Mandatory notification of all school authorities upon visit
options.C: Strict adult-only operating hours on weekday mornings
options.D: Guaranteed confidentiality and non-judgmental staff attitude

explanation: Teens are more likely to seek help if they know their privacy is protected and staff will not judge them. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h7)

question: How do airborne gases and fumes mostly enter the body?

options.A: Parenteral injection
options.B: Dermal absorption
options.C: Inhalation
options.D: Ingestion

explanation: Airborne fumes and gases enter through the respiratory tract and quickly cross into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T8#GNS215_U5_T8_h1)

question: Why is the World Health Organization definition of health important for communities?

options.A: It includes physical, mental, and social wellness dimensions
options.B: It measures the financial wealth of a given population
options.C: It prioritizes urban development over rural health centers
options.D: It focuses solely on treating infectious diseases in hospitals

explanation: The holistic definition ensures that community health programs address social and mental needs alongside physical ailments. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T5#GNS225_U1_T5_h1)

question: Why is needle recapping strongly discouraged in clinical guidelines?

options.A: It wastes valuable time during busy shifts
options.B: It violates the manufacturer's warranty
options.C: It increases the risk of needle-stick injuries
options.D: It bends the needle tip making it useless

explanation: Trying to guide a used needle back into its cap frequently leads to missed caps and finger punctures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h5)

question: A community health nurse arrives at a new IDP settlement; what is the first priority?

options.A: Distribute personal clothing items
options.B: Build permanent brick houses
options.C: Conduct a rapid environmental and health needs assessment
options.D: Organize a major surgical camp

explanation: Before planning interventions, nurses must assess immediate risks, population size, and existing health threats. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T20#GNS225_U5_T20_h4)

question: A patient with severe neutropenia is admitted to the ward. Which nursing intervention is most appropriate?

options.A: Administering live attenuated viral vaccines to stimulate immunity
options.B: Placing fresh flowers in the room to brighten the clinical environment
options.C: Implementing strict protective isolation to minimize pathogen exposure
options.D: Encouraging frequent family visits to boost the patient's emotional state

explanation: Neutropenic patients lack sufficient neutrophils, requiring barrier precautions to protect them from environmental microbes. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T2#GNS123_U4_T2_h7)

question: What tool should a nurse use to fill gaps between the patient's body and the mattress?

options.A: Plastic boards or hard trays
options.B: Tight cotton binding sheets
options.C: Extra heavy woolen blankets
options.D: Pillows, rolls, or wedges

explanation: Support devices like pillows distribute weight evenly and maintain natural body contours. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T8#GNS112_U4_T8_h2)

question: What does the letter 'Q' stand for in the PQRSTU pain assessment mnemonic?

options.A: Quality
options.B: Quietness
options.C: Quickness
options.D: Quantity

explanation: The letter Q asks about the quality or character of the pain, such as sharp, dull, or aching. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T2#GNS123_U3_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary basis for classifying drugs by formation?

options.A: The specific organ system they target
options.B: Their therapeutic effect on the body
options.C: The speed at which they are metabolized
options.D: Their source or method of manufacture

explanation: Classification by formation categorizes medications based on their origin or how they are produced, ranging from natural sources to laboratory synthesis. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h1)

question: How should a patient properly clean their residual limb during daily hygiene routines?

options.A: Apply medicated petroleum jelly and wrap tightly
options.B: Soak the limb in hot water for at least one hour
options.C: Wash with mild soap and warm water, then pat dry
options.D: Scrub vigorously with a stiff brush and antiseptic

explanation: Gentle cleansing prevents skin irritation, and thorough drying stops moisture accumulation that attracts bacterial or fungal infections. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T12#GNS324_U4_T12_h4)

question: What serious kidney problem is linked to certain strains of E. coli food poisoning?

options.A: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome
options.B: Glomerular nephritis
options.C: Polycystic kidney disease
options.D: Chronic pyelonephritis

explanation: Certain E. coli toxins destroy red blood cells and damage tiny blood vessels in the kidneys, leading to Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h7)

question: Driving through a neighborhood to observe housing conditions and drainage systems is known as what type of assessment tool?

options.A: Surgical audit
options.B: Pharmacological trial
options.C: Windshield survey
options.D: Laboratory biopsy

explanation: A windshield survey is an observational method where the nurse assesses community features while traveling through the area. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T26#GNS225_U2_T26_h5)

question: Why must a nurse researcher submit their quantitative proposal to an ethics committee?

options.A: To secure funding for laboratory equipment and supplies.
options.B: To speed up the final publication process in medical journals.
options.C: To safeguard the rights and welfare of human participants.
options.D: To guarantee that the study will achieve statistical significance.

explanation: Ethics committees independently review protocols to ensure participants are protected from undue harm, exploitation, or coercion. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T4#GNS224_U1_T4_h8)

question: Why do stable clients return downward from tertiary hospitals to primary health centres?

options.A: To free up hospital beds for surgical emergency cases
options.B: To receive routine method resupply closer to their homes
options.C: To undergo mandatory re-evaluation of their medical history
options.D: To comply with restrictions on long-term tertiary clinic visits

explanation: De-escalating stable clients reduces facility congestion and brings basic resupply services closer to the community. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h3)

question: How can a nursing student best avoid common mistakes in their research proposal?

options.A: By seeking peer review and carefully checking guidelines
options.B: By avoiding the methodology section entirely
options.C: By copying another student's completed study verbatim
options.D: By submitting the document without reading through it

explanation: Reviewing guidelines and getting feedback from colleagues catches errors before official submission. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T1#GNS224_U3_T1_h7)

question: Where does decision-making power lie in a heavily centralized nursing service?

options.A: At the top executive management level
options.B: Among individual patient advocacy groups
options.C: With the frontline bedside staff nurses
options.D: Directly with the junior ward attendants

explanation: Centralisation keeps authority concentrated with senior administrators at the top of the organizational chart. [learn more](GST321_U1_T9#GST321_U1_T9_h6)

question: A farmer gets sick after liquid insecticide soaks through his work clothes. What route of exposure happened here?

options.A: Inhalation exposure
options.B: Parenteral injection
options.C: Dermal absorption
options.D: Gastrointestinal ingestion

explanation: Liquid chemicals can pass through the skin barrier directly into the bloodstream, especially when protective gear is absent. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T5#GNS112_U7_T5_h2)

question: Reducing patient wait times and speeding up bed turnover rates target what aspect of healthcare?

options.A: Personal career growth
options.B: Operational efficiency
options.C: Individual salary structures
options.D: Staff holiday planning

explanation: Streamlining processes like bed turnover and wait times directly improves the operational flow of the facility. [learn more](GST321_U2_T2#GST321_U2_T2_h3)

question: When is an MRI preferred over a CT scan for EENT evaluations?

options.A: When the patient cannot lie flat
options.B: When detailed soft tissue and nerve pathways need viewing
options.C: When checking for metal objects
options.D: When checking for acute bone fractures after an accident

explanation: MRI excels at showing soft tissue details, such as the optic nerve or brain structures, without radiation exposure. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T2#GNS311_U3_T2_h6)

question: What term describes the entire group of individuals that a researcher wants to generalize findings to?

options.A: Target population
options.B: Control group
options.C: Pilot cohort
options.D: Sample subset

explanation: The target population represents the complete set of cases or individuals meeting the inclusion criteria of the study. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T2#GNS224_U3_T2_h6)

question: Skin traction is most commonly used in clinical practice as which type of intervention?

options.A: A long-term outpatient rehabilitation exercise program
options.B: An emergency treatment for severe head injuries
options.C: A temporary measure before definitive surgical repair
options.D: A permanent substitute for open reduction internal fixation

explanation: Hospitals use skin traction to stabilize limbs while patients await surgery or until swelling subsides. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T8#GNS221_U1_T8_h2)

question: Which professional should a nurse contact first when a patient exhibits frequent coughing while swallowing food?

options.A: Hospital administrator
options.B: Chief pharmacist
options.C: Radiology technician
options.D: Speech-language pathologist

explanation: Speech therapists specialize in swallowing disorders and perform assessments to prevent aspiration risks. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h3)

question: How do international donor agencies primarily support Nigeria's family planning goals?

options.A: Replacing local nursing staff with expatriate clinicians
options.B: Enforcing strict population control laws in rural states
options.C: Providing financial backing and commodity procurement support
options.D: Taking over the direct governance of teaching hospitals

explanation: Donors assist the government by funding the purchase and supply chain management of contraceptive commodities to prevent stock-outs. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h4)

question: What is the primary function of a cerumenolytic ear drop?

options.A: To soften and break up impacted earwax
options.B: To dry up excessive fluid drainage from otitis
options.C: To numb the tympanic membrane for surgery
options.D: To kill bacterial pathogens in the middle ear

explanation: Cerumenolytics break down hard earwax so it can be safely removed from the external auditory canal. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h6)

question: Why is epidemiological data essential for community health nurses?

options.A: It eliminates the need for patient communication
options.B: It guides evidence-based planning and resource distribution
options.C: It proves which nurses work the fastest hours
options.D: It guarantees complete eradication of all global illnesses

explanation: Epidemiological data shows where diseases strike hardest, allowing nurses to deploy resources where they are most needed. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T8#GNS225_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why must a patient avoid swallowing a sublingual nitroglycerin tablet?

options.A: It will cause immediate severe stomach ulcers
options.B: Stomach acids will destroy the active drug
options.C: It binds permanently to the stomach lining
options.D: Swallowing speeds up systemic absorption too much

explanation: Swallowing sublingual tablets exposes them to stomach acid and liver breakdown, making them largely ineffective. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h6)

question: Why is inducing vomiting discouraged in patients who swallowed corrosive substances?

options.A: It immediately triggers irreversible cardiac arrest in all patients
options.B: It neutralizes the antidote before it can be administered
options.C: It causes secondary chemical burns to the esophagus and increases aspiration risks
options.D: It forces the toxin to move faster into the large intestine

explanation: Brings corrosive substances back up re-exposes the delicate esophageal tissue to burning and raises the danger of fluid entering the lungs. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h5)

question: What is the main difference between nursing research and evidence-based practice?

options.A: There is no difference between the two terms
options.B: Research is done at the bedside while EBP is done in a laboratory
options.C: Research generates new knowledge while EBP applies existing findings
options.D: EBP is only performed by doctors while research is for nurses

explanation: Research discovers facts, whereas evidence-based practice uses those discovered facts to improve daily nursing care. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which nursing action directly neutralizes a human source of bacterial infection?

options.A: Applying hand sanitizer after meals
options.B: Educating patients on balanced diets
options.C: Placing surgical masks on visitors
options.D: Administering prescribed antibiotics

explanation: Effective antimicrobial therapy kills the pathogen within the human source, stopping active shedding. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T7#GNS313_U1_T7_h6)

question: A patient complains of sharp pain in the right lower abdominal quadrant. Which organ is most likely involved?

options.A: Appendix
options.B: Stomach
options.C: Spleen
options.D: Gallbladder

explanation: The appendix is typically located in the right lower quadrant, making it the primary organ suspected during localized pain in that area. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h5)

question: A major direct cause of maternal mortality in Nigeria is...

options.A: Early childhood malnutrition
options.B: Severe postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Chronic childhood asthma
options.D: Gestational diabetes mellitus

explanation: Bleeding after childbirth is one of the leading direct medical causes of maternal death in the region. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T001#GNS226_U1_T001_h2)

question: A nurse finishes scrubbing and accidentally touches an unsterile tap with the elbow. What should be done?

options.A: Repeat the entire surgical hand scrub from the beginning
options.B: Proceed to gowning since elbows are outside the sterile field
options.C: Rinse only the contaminated elbow thoroughly with sterile saline
options.D: Wipe the affected elbow with alcohol-soaked cotton

explanation: Any break in technique compromises sterility, requiring a full repeat scrub to ensure patient safety. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h3)

question: How does a literature review assist in shaping a new research question?

options.A: By dictating the exact hospital ward where the study must happen
options.B: By providing the final conclusion before data collection starts
options.C: By eliminating the need for any statistical testing
options.D: By revealing ambiguities and contradictions in previous studies

explanation: Unresolved questions or conflicting findings in existing literature point the way for new, meaningful research questions. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T5#GNS217_U3_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary clinical goal of prescribing antiepileptic drugs to a patient with epilepsy?

options.A: To lower blood pressure and improve overall heart rhythm
options.B: To sedate the patient so they sleep through the night
options.C: To permanently cure the underlying brain tissue damage
options.D: To raise the seizure threshold and stabilize neuronal firing

explanation: AEDs work by dampening excessive electrical excitability in the central nervous system. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h7)

question: What is a primary nursing responsibility after resuscitation efforts are formally terminated?

options.A: Supporting grieving family members and upholding patient dignity
options.B: Immediately discharging the room for the next hospital admission
options.C: Notifying the hospital finance department to cancel billing accounts
options.D: Disposing of all patient medical records to protect confidentiality

explanation: Compassionate post-mortem care and family support are core ethical duties for nurses when a life cannot be saved. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T7#GNS321_U2_T7_h9)

question: Promoting education for the girl child helps achieve population policy goals by doing what?

options.A: Eliminating the need for maternal health clinics
options.B: Naturally delaying marriage and encouraging smaller family sizes
options.C: Forcing young girls to migrate to urban centers
options.D: Increasing the infant mortality rate in rural areas

explanation: Educated women tend to marry later and make informed choices about family spacing and size. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T007#GNS226_U6_T007_h2)

question: Which major complication should a nurse watch out for after a major cancer surgery?

options.A: Venous thromboembolism
options.B: Permanent systemic hair loss
options.C: Immunotherapy toxicity
options.D: Acute radiation dermatitis

explanation: Having cancer and undergoing major surgery both raise the risk of blood clots forming in the deep veins. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T10#GNS321_U1_T10_h2)

question: Who is primarily responsible for monitoring daily medication side effects in an inpatient ward?

options.A: The occupational therapist
options.B: The facility administrator
options.C: The hospital accountant
options.D: The psychiatric nurse

explanation: Nurses spend the most time with patients and observe immediate responses and side effects to prescribed drugs. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T2#GNS314_U1_T2_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT allowed for clinical nurses to maintain hand hygiene safety?

options.A: Artificial fingernails
options.B: Plain metal wedding bands
options.C: Hospital-approved hand lotion
options.D: Short natural nails

explanation: Artificial nails harbor high concentrations of fungi and bacteria that resist standard hand washing and easily transfer to patients. [learn more](GST114_U2_T6#GST114_U2_T6_h8)

question: How does medication counselling differ from simply administering a drug to a patient?

options.A: Administration requires no physical contact with the patient
options.B: Counselling involves teaching and active patient participation
options.C: Administration covers long term side effect management
options.D: Counselling is performed exclusively by hospital pharmacists

explanation: Giving a drug is a physical task, whereas counselling educates the patient to manage their therapy independently. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h1)

question: Why do nurse researchers use inferential statistics like the t-test?

options.A: To summarize the basic demographics of the ward
options.B: To check if study results happened by chance
options.C: To replace the need for ethical committee approval
options.D: To list the qualitative feedback from patients

explanation: Inferential statistics help determine if an intervention caused a real difference rather than random variation. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T14#GNS217_U4_T14_h1)
